title: Explain a moving tangent
summary: Explain a moving tangent by connecting a plotted function, a tracker and a derivative.
outcome: A moving point and tangent line that remain connected to the same function.

blocks.text: Keep the tangent on the curve
Explore how a tangent changes along a curve. First plot the function, then animate a point with one scalar tracker, and finally let the pointer choose the point whose slope you want to inspect.
1. Give the curve a coordinate system
We will show how the tangent changes along y = x² / 2. `Axes` defines the mathematical range and its physical size; `FunctionGraph2D` creates the curve.
Keep the formula named once as `f`. That avoids using slightly different equations for the graph and the later tangent. Change the plotted domain and inspect the curve before animating it.
A `ValueTracker` stores x. Its animation moves x from −2 to 2, and a post updater places the dot at `Axes.c2p(x, f(x))`.
The tracker carries mathematical data; the dot carries visible geometry. This separation lets the same x drive a label, tangent or projection line without independent animations drifting apart.

The final version estimates slope with a centered difference and constructs a short tangent segment in mathematical coordinates. Both endpoints pass through `Axes.c2p`, keeping them aligned with the plotted axes.

After the initial sweep, move the pointer across the preview to select x. `Axes.p2c` returns a coordinate pair, and clamping keeps the point within the useful domain. Change h from 0.01 to 0.5 to inspect approximation error.
Use it in your own application
The centered difference is an approximation. For this quadratic the derivative is x; replace the estimate with x and compare them before trying a less simple function.
Handle domain boundaries, discontinuities and nonfinite function values explicitly. A tangent near a singularity may need to be omitted rather than drawn with invalid coordinates.
